description:
Say what changed in a service's policy since a date, expressed as changes to the eight fixed answers.

You cannot do this yourself at any context size: it needs the earlier version of the document, and the earlier version is gone from the web. Policy Pal keeps the eight answers for every version it has read, so the difference is a fact rather than a reconstruction.

It reports answer changes -- for example forced arbitration moving from no to yes -- and not text edits. A changed comma is noise; a changed answer is the thing worth telling someone about.

Returns nothing to report when the answers are unchanged, and says so explicitly when it has no reading from before that date rather than guessing. A question the earlier reading did not answer is reported as not compared, never as not_stated. Automated reading of one document. Not legal advice.

since.description: The date you last looked, as YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO timestamp. The answer is the difference between what was true then and what is true now.

url.description: The https address of the published policy page.
